Clean Energy RNG station-economics slide ($/GGE, federal/state credits, station buildout cost)
UPS 2025/2035/2050 sustainability-goals timeline and global alt-fuel fleet composition

title: Messy Middle Bootcamp #2 – Decarbonizing with Natural Gas
abstract: NACFE's Run on Less Messy Middle Bootcamp Session 2, held February 25, 2025, the second session of the diesel/natural-gas unit. Moderated by Rachel Ellenberger with an update from Mike Roeth, Matt Tomich (Energy Vision) covers renewable natural gas production, economics, and nationwide project growth; Dan Deppeler (Paper Transport/PTI) and Marty Tufte (WM) each detail their companies' CNG/RNG fleet adoption, infrastructure, and emissions results; and Dave King (Cummins) introduces the newly launched X15N heavy-duty natural gas engine and its integration with Cummins' Endurant transmission lineup.
key_findings: WM operates more than 13,000 Class 8 natural gas trucks across 213 self-built fueling stations (25 public), has invested over $4 billion, and displaced 110 million gallons of diesel in 2024, with over 75% of its routed fleet on natural gas (45% of that RNG).
WM said 54 trucks operating at 1985 emissions levels produced as much total NOx as 1,080 trucks running WM's 2018-standard natural gas engines.

Energy Vision reported 897 RNG production facilities nationwide (443 operational, 170 under construction, 285 planned), up more than tenfold from about 60 in 2017; Paper Transport, natural-gas-fueled since 2008, has surpassed 77 million natural gas miles and puts its CNG-vs-diesel breakeven around 200,000 miles per truck.
data_available: WM CNG fleet stats slide (vehicle counts, fueling stations, investment, technician/driver training)
WM RNG operations slide (facility counts, DGE volume, carbon-intensity score)
NOx emissions historical comparison chart, 1985 vs. 2027 EPA standards
Paper Transport 15-year natural-gas history slide (miles, diesel displaced, breakeven mileage)
Cummins X15N engine reliability/spec slide

title: Messy Middle Bootcamp #1 – Diesel Drop-In Alternatives: Ultra-Low Sulfur, Bio-, and Renewable
abstract: NACFE's Run on Less Messy Middle Bootcamp Session 1, held February 11, 2025, opening the diesel/natural-gas unit and the whole bootcamp series. Moderated by Rachel Ellenberger with an update from Mike Roeth, NACFE's Jeff Seger covers the upcoming EPA 2027 low-NOx engine rule and the two competing aftertreatment architectures being adopted by engine makers; Scott Fenwick (Clean Fuels Alliance America) and Colin Huyeler (Optimus Technologies) cover biodiesel/renewable-diesel market growth and drop-in retrofit technology; and Andrew Gibson (Shell) covers low-viscosity lubricants.
key_findings: The EPA 2027 rule cuts the heavy-duty NOx limit from 0.2 to 0.035 g/bhp-hr; Cummins, PACCAR, and Volvo are adopting a heater-based aftertreatment architecture (Volvo adding a 48V battery), while International is using a dual-SCR/dual-dosing design without an EGR cooler on its S13 engine.

Clean Fuels Alliance America reported US biomass-based diesel consumption reached a record 4.9-5.1 billion gallons in 2024 (up from roughly 250 million gallons about 15 years earlier), with California's low-carbon fuel standard pushing biodiesel/renewable diesel to 70-75% of the state's diesel pool by mid-2024.

Optimus Technologies said its Vector dual-fuel system, which auto-switches engines to 100% biodiesel after startup on diesel, has over 1,100 Class 8 trucks in service with more than 85 million miles logged, validated to below -30°F and in a 1.3-million-mile joint study with ADM Trucking.
data_available: EPA NOx regulation history chart (1991-2027) and OEM aftertreatment architecture diagrams (Cummins/PACCAR/Volvo vs. International)
US biomass-based diesel consumption chart, 2011-2025, and biodiesel policy-by-state map
Optimus Vector system diagram and B100 retail-station rollout map (Pilot Flying J, Q1 2025)

title: Stories from the Run: The Future
abstract: NACFE 'Stories from the Run' montage from the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle campaign, splicing brief on-camera reflections from fleets, OEMs, and infrastructure providers (Ben Sharpe, Bill Zobel/Pilot, Brad Bayne/4Gen Logistics, Lori Clark/DFW Clean Cities, Henry Albert, and others) on where diesel, natural gas, battery-electric, and hydrogen truck technology is headed.
key_findings: 4Gen Logistics VP Brad Bayne says the fleet's goal is to be completely zero-emission by the end of 2025, with no plans to add diesel equipment.
Pilot's Bill Zobel expects hydrogen fuel cell tractor fuel economy to keep improving as fuel cell stack technology matures, helping drive further adoption.

title: Stories from the Run: Sustainability
abstract: NACFE 'Stories from the Run' clip from the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle campaign, gathering short interviews with fleet and OEM leaders (4Gen Logistics, UPS, Cummins, Wegmans, Windrose, Dallas-Fort Worth Clean Cities, and others) on why they are pursuing decarbonization and their sustainability commitments.
key_findings: UPS's Nathan Branch cites a goal of a 50% reduction in small-package-operation CO2 emissions by 2035 and 100% renewable-energy-fueled US operations.
Cummins' Jelena Rowe says the company's technologies displaced 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 in 2024 and Cummins is committed to net zero by 2050.

title: Stories from the Run: TCO
abstract: NACFE 'Stories from the Run' clip from the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle campaign, in which fleet executives, OEM reps, and analysts (Rob Reich, Henry Albert, Wegmans' Matt Harris, Windrose's Mark Duchesne, and others) discuss how total cost of ownership drives adoption decisions across diesel, RNG, and electric powertrains.
key_findings: Wegmans' Matt Harris reports an ROI of about two to two-and-a-half years for its renewable natural gas trucks versus diesel, based on five-year average diesel pricing.
Windrose's Mark Duchesne says the company designed its business model around receiving no subsidies, arguing the technology and economics must work without outside support.

title: Stories from the Run: Duty Cycle Matters
abstract: NACFE 'Stories from the Run' clip from the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle campaign, in which fleet and OEM voices (Lori Clark, Wegmans' Matt Harris, Pilot's Bill Zobel, Kleysen Group's Phil Rivard, and others) explain why powertrain choice must be matched to a fleet's specific duty cycle rather than applied as a one-size-fits-all solution.
key_findings: Wegmans partnered with Windrose for a battery-electric truck offering up to 420 miles of range to fit its target duty-cycle 'Goldilocks zone.'
Pilot's Bill Zobel says the company has run five Hyundai hydrogen fuel cell trucks for almost a year with strong performance and no issues.

title: Stories from the Run: The Importance of Data
abstract: NACFE 'Stories from the Run' clip from the 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle campaign, featuring fleet and telematics-provider voices (Geotab, Tesla, Cummins, UPS, JoyRide Logistics, Nevoya, and others) on how data -- state of charge, range, ECM data, GPS -- drives fleet decisions across powertrains.
key_findings: JoyRide Logistics' Brian Birge says about 98% of the fleet's operations/dispatch staff work remotely from Bosnia, coordinating trucks via real-time GPS.
Nevoya's John Vernon describes building a proprietary EV- and AI-native transportation management system to manage range, battery state of charge, and charging logistics.

title: Penske: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Penske Logistics running a Hyundai Xcient hydrogen fuel cell tractor out of Lancaster, TX, hauling Hyundai Mobis auto parts to over 300 Hyundai/Kia/Genesis dealers across the Southwest. Covers mobile hydrogen refueling infrastructure and driver experience.
key_findings: Penske Logistics is a $4.3 billion company operating almost 11,000 drivers, 8,000+ tractors, and about 22,000 trailers; the Lancaster, TX facility services over 300 dealers from Mississippi to El Paso to Wyoming.

Because Texas lacks hydrogen fueling stations, Penske and HydroFleet built a mobile, self-contained refueling trailer that compresses medium-pressure hydrogen up to 13,500 PSI and can refuel about six trucks before needing to be recharged.

title: Kleysen Group: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Kleysen Group (part of Mullen Group), based in Edmonton, Alberta, running a Kenworth T880 sleeper with a Cummins X15N natural gas engine hauling bulk liquids into far-north Alberta in extreme temperatures, on roughly 500-600 mile round trips.
key_findings: Kleysen operates a roughly 250-tractor fleet and was first to market with the Cummins X15N natural gas engine in 2024; the truck has run without complaint from -30C to 30-35C temperatures.
The truck carries a 244-inch wheelbase with a 175-diesel-gallon-equivalent Cummins clean fuel tank; natural gas refueling takes a maximum of 15 minutes.

title: Mesilla Valley Transportation: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Mesilla Valley Transportation (MVT), an El Paso, TX carrier and repeat Run on Less participant (also in 2017), running an International LT with a Cummins X15 diesel engine. Focuses on the fleet's long-standing culture of driver-driven fuel-economy discipline.
key_findings: CEO Royal Jones says the fleet's company-wide average is 9.20 MPG, after ELD-mandate and emissions changes had dropped it to about 8.3 from a prior peak near 9.4.
Driver Roberto Sandoval says trucks can run up to 2,000 miles on a single fueling, and MVT is field-testing Cummins' next-generation beta EPA27 engine.

title: Schneider: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Schneider in Phoenix, AZ, running an International LT S13 integrated powertrain on a route to California. Covers Schneider's roughly 13,000-truck fleet, fuel-optimization strategy, driver-assist technology, and the S13's emissions-focused clean-sheet engine design.
key_findings: Schneider operates about 10,000 company trucks plus 2,000 owner-operators, approaching 13,000 Class 8 vehicles with acquisitions; over 90% of its fuel is purchased through Pilot using a fuel-optimizer tool.

International's Dan Simnick says the S13 delivers six to eight percent better fuel economy than a comparable diesel engine by eliminating an EGR cooler, diesel oxidation catalyst, and seventh injector.

title: Frito-Lay: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Frito-Lay's Topeka, KS plant, which distributes snacks from Montana to South Texas using a Volvo VNL tractor equipped with an Optimus dual-tank B100 biodiesel system, alongside its existing CNG and battery-electric tractors. Covers biodiesel infrastructure, aero devices, and maintenance.
key_findings: Of roughly 120 pieces of equipment at the Topeka site, all but 10 run on natural gas, battery-electric, or biodiesel; the Optimus system runs the truck on up to 100% B100 for about 85-90% of the duty cycle, starting and stopping on diesel.

Frito-Lay has expanded biodiesel infrastructure from one site in 2022 to about seven sites and roughly 700 biodiesel-capable assets; aero add-ons like Truck Wings and Flow Below are cited as yielding about a 4.5% fuel-economy gain (5.88 gallons per 1,000 miles).

title: UPS: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of UPS's Salt Lake City, UT regional hub, running a Kenworth T680 daycab with a Cummins X15N natural gas engine across mountainous Utah terrain. Covers the hub's high CNG adoption, maintenance differences versus diesel, and range/infrastructure constraints.
key_findings: 92% of the package fleet at this UPS building runs on CNG, and 65% of the Salt Lake City fleet overall is natural gas; about 240 drivers a day go out of the facility, which planned for natural gas from its opening seven years ago.

The Procab natural gas fuel system holds 175 diesel-gallon-equivalents for a 700-800 mile range; mechanics report more frequent valve adjustments and spark plug wear versus diesel but otherwise comparable maintenance.

title: JoyRide Logistics: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of JoyRide Logistics in Phoenix, AZ, running a Windrose battery-electric sleeper tractor across its Southwest US regional-haul network, where drivers return home every other night. Covers Windrose's battery architecture, charging, and driver feedback.
key_findings: JoyRide needed a truck delivering close to 400 miles of range with a sleeper; Windrose's tractor delivers 420 miles and recently reached 772 kW charging at a Greenlane site.
The tractor's four battery packs total 705 kWh, built into a frame designed around the battery box rather than retrofit into a standard diesel ladder frame.

title: Albert Transport: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of owner-operator Henry Albert (Albert Transport), a repeat Run on Less participant (also 2017), running a 2022 Freightliner Cascadia with a Detroit DD15 diesel engine. Details the truck's extensive aerodynamic spec and Daimler's fifth-generation Cascadia updates.
key_findings: Henry Albert reports a lifetime average of 10.5 MPG over 459,000 miles on this truck, recently hitting close to 12.5 MPG in a month; the DD15 is rated 455 hp and 1,850 lb-ft at 950 RPM.

Daimler's Riley Elizabeth Holland says Cascadia fuel economy has improved over 35% since 2007, with the fifth-generation model (launched mid-2025) adding 1.9% from aerodynamic changes alone, including a new hood-to-bumper seal and three-piece wheel-well closeout.

title: Nevoya: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Nevoya, a fully electric truckload carrier, running a Freightliner eCascadia out of Greenlane's new Colton, CA charging facility to serve LA-region shippers, supplemented by port drayage and rail work. Covers Nevoya's EV/AI-native TMS and the Greenlane charging site build-out.
key_findings: Nevoya's trucks currently run 180-225 miles of range depending on payload, serving SoCal, Northern California, and Dallas, TX out of the Colton site sitting at the I-10/I-15 intersection.

The Greenlane Colton site has 29 bobtail chargers and 12 400-kilowatt pull-through lane chargers, using ABB Emax 2 low-voltage breakers and a modular medium-voltage system for future megawatt charging.

title: 4Gen: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of 4Gen Logistics in Rialto, CA, a drayage fleet serving the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach with 40 Volvo VNR Electric tractors in two-shift operations. Covers charging strategy, driver adaptation, and 4Gen's goal of zero-emission port operations by end of 2025.
key_findings: 4Gen runs its VNR Electric fleet in two-shift operations getting over 200 miles per day per vehicle using on-site 350-kilowatt chargers at Rialto and Long Beach, after starting BEV operations over two and a half years ago.
4Gen is expanding Rialto charging capacity to 30 dispensers and doubling Long Beach to 60 dispensers, originally targeted for end of 2026 but now expected around 2027 due to grant delays.

title: Saia: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Saia LTL Freight in Stockton, CA, running two Tesla Semi tractors within its 7,000-truck, 213-terminal LTL network, used for both linehaul runs and city pickup-and-delivery (P&D) 'double duty' shifts.
key_findings: One Saia Tesla Semi is used for both an overnight linehaul run and a city P&D route the next morning; the tractor is capped at charging to 80% (about 45 minutes from 5%) since that proved the best time/range tradeoff.

Driver Michael Davis reports roughly a 500-mile battery range that drops considerably in windy conditions; Tesla says it is transitioning from small-volume pilot production to a high-volume Nevada factory.

title: Pilot: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: NACFE Run on Less – Messy Middle fleet profile of Pilot (Pilot Travel Centers) in Rialto, CA, running one of five Hyundai Xcient hydrogen fuel cell trucks to deliver hydrogen fuel across Southern California in 24/7 slip-seat operation.
key_findings: Hyundai's Benjamin Happek says the truck pairs two 85 kW fuel cell systems and a 72 kWh battery to drive a 350 kW e-motor, with a real-world range of about 430-510 miles and a 70 kg/700-bar (about 10,000 psi) hydrogen tank system.

Driver Dave Bickmeier improved his fuel efficiency from 5.9 to 9.1 miles per kilogram of hydrogen through driving technique; Pilot runs the trucks 24/7 via driver slip-seating since there's no charging downtime.

title: Wegmans: Run on Less – Messy Middle Fleet Profile
abstract: Fleet profile of Wegmans' CNG Class 8 tractor fleet (76% non-diesel, targeting 100% by 2026) filmed in Rochester, NY for Run on Less Messy Middle. Covers Cummins 15L natural gas engine (X15N/HELM), Chevron renewable natural gas fueling, driver feedback, and operational considerations like idle time and range.
key_findings: Wegmans' Class 8 tractor fleet was 76% diesel-free (natural gas) at time of filming, with a goal of reaching 100% non-diesel by 2026.
The natural gas tractors have roughly 500-mile-per-day range using Cummins 12L and 15L engines with Allison transmissions, enabling tandem-trailer hauls up to 140,000 lbs to Erie and Boston.
data_available: 76% non-diesel fleet share
500-mile CNG tractor daily range
75C reduction in engine top-side temperature (Cummins 12N/15N vs. prior design)

title: Regional Stories – Hydrogen Technology Day
abstract: NACFE Technology Day webinar (October 8, 2019) exploring whether hydrogen fuel cells are a viable Class 8 truck fuel, with panelists from Kenworth/Toyota, Nikola, Shell, and NREL. Discusses hydrogen's fit for routes over 300 miles beyond battery-electric range, diesel-comparable refueling times, and infrastructure/standards challenges.
key_findings: Kenworth and Toyota are building the first of 10 hydrogen fuel cell electric Class 8 tractors as part of their partnership.

Panelists positioned hydrogen as suited to routes over 300 miles where battery-electric range and charging time become limiting, citing refueling times closer to diesel than to battery-electric charging.
data_available: Nikola's planned 8-ton/day hydrogen station capacity

title: Regional Stories – Electric Truck Technology Day
abstract: Audio-only NACFE Technology Day webinar (October 2019) asking how far battery-electric trucks can go, previewing NACFE's fourth electric guidance report on heavy-duty tractors. Panelists from NFI Industries, Daimler Trucks, Meritor, and Southern California Edison discuss suited duty cycles, charging infrastructure as the biggest barrier, and battery cost trends.
key_findings: NACFE identifies P&D medium duty, dock spotters, and school buses as the duty cycles best suited to battery-electric trucks today, with urban routes (under 250 miles) as the target range.
Panelists projected 10-15% market penetration for battery-electric trucks within five years if battery cost trends continue, growing further over the following 15-20 years.
data_available: Projected 10-15% BEV market penetration within 5 years
100,000+ Class 8 trucks sold annually for urban routes under 250 miles

title: Regional Stories – Connectivity Technology Day
abstract: NACFE Technology Day webinar (October 15, 2019) on whether connectivity can improve trucking efficiency, with panelists from LinkeDrive, PepsiCo, Cummins, Peloton, and Noodle.ai discussing telematics data, truck platooning, over-the-air engine tuning, and predictive maintenance to reduce downtime.
key_findings: Panelists described connectivity applications including real-time truck-weight monitoring (PepsiCo), over-the-air engine customization (Cummins), closer-following truck platooning (Peloton), and predictive maintenance using sensor data like coolant temperature to flag failures before they cause downtime (Noodle.ai).

title: Run on Less 2017 – Mike Roeth and Dave Schaller Introduction
abstract: NACFE's Mike Roeth and Dave Schaller introduce the 2017 Run on Less kickoff, covering the seven participating drivers/fleets, the Geotab telematics harness capturing speed/elevation/fuel/mileage data streamed to runonless.com, and the 85 tracked efficiency technologies that vary across the diverse truck specs.
key_findings: Seven fleets and drivers (Mesilla Valley, Ploger, Hirschbach, Nussbaum, Frito-Lay, US Xpress, Albert Transport) were instrumented with Geotab telematics devices tracking vehicle speed, elevation, gallons burned, and miles traveled, streamed live to runonless.com.
NACFE tracked 85 distinct fuel-efficiency technologies across the trucks, with no single common spec set -- fleets varied in tires, trailer aerodynamics, and powertrains.
data_available: List of tracked efficiency technology categories (85 total)
Real-time per-truck telematics metrics (speed, elevation, fuel, miles)

title: Electric DEPOT – ACT Expo Roundup 2023
abstract: Roundup video from ACT Expo 2023 in Anaheim introducing the eight depots participating in Run on Less Electric DEPOT. Fleet and OEM representatives, including PepsiCo discussing its new Tesla Semi, cover charger-to-truck ratios, planned MCS charging, and depot electrification strategy.
key_findings: Eight depots are participating in Run on Less Electric DEPOT, introduced to the industry at ACT Expo 2023.

One site plans to deploy 15 electric route trucks using only 10 chargers, showcasing a less-than-one-to-one charger-to-truck ratio; another plans to charge 92 trucks via 16 dispensers with 32 charging cords.
data_available: Depot count (8) and per-site truck/charger ratios (e.g. 15 trucks/10 chargers; 92 trucks/16 dispensers/32 cords)

title: Electric DEPOT – May 2023 Roundup
abstract: Companion roundup video (same panel commentary as the ACT Expo cut, without the expo framing) introducing the eight depots in Run on Less Electric DEPOT. Fleet and OEM voices, including PepsiCo on its Tesla Semi partnership, discuss charger-to-truck ratios and depot charging strategy.
key_findings: Eight depots are participating in Run on Less Electric DEPOT.
One site plans 15 electric route trucks with only 10 chargers; another plans to charge 92 trucks via 16 dispensers with 32 charging cords.
data_available: Per-site truck/charger ratios (e.g. 15 trucks/10 chargers; 92 trucks/16 dispensers/32 cords)

title: 2017 Stories – Wind
abstract: Short thematic segment on how wind affects fuel economy in the 2017 Run on Less. NACFE's Dave Schaller notes trailer tails and aerodynamic tractors mitigate crosswinds, while drivers Clark Reed (Nussbaum) and Henry Albert (Albert Transport) share anecdotes about tailwind MPG gains and a risky high-wind crossing in Wyoming caused by inaccurate load-weight paperwork.
key_findings: Dave Schaller cites roughly a 13% drop in fuel economy for a 10 mph increase in headwind, and notes losing about half a mile per gallon when running without a trailer tail.

Henry Albert (Albert Transport) recorded a 1.5 MPG boost from tailwinds on September 9, 2017; Nussbaum driver Clark Reed described a hazardous high-wind crossing of I-80 in Wyoming caused by inaccurate bill-of-lading weight information.
data_available: ~13% MPG drop per 10 mph headwind increase (Schaller estimate)
~0.5 MPG loss without trailer tail
1.5 MPG tailwind boost (Albert Transport, Sept 9 2017)

title: Run on Less 2017 – TV Coverage
abstract: Local Fort Wayne NBC-affiliate news segment covering the September 2017 Run on Less campaign kickoff, with reporter Kent Hormann interviewing NACFE's Mike Roeth and Dave Schaller about the campaign's goal of showcasing high-MPG Class 8 tractor-trailers and the technologies (aerodynamics, electronics, idle reduction) driving efficiency gains.
key_findings: Mike Roeth states there are 1.7 million Class 8 trucks in the US and the industry spends about $75 billion annually on fuel for them; NACFE tracks 85 efficiency technologies across the fleet.
Dave Schaller notes typical historical diesel fuel economy of 6.5-7 MPG, with the Run on Less trucks expected to run well north of 9 MPG.
data_available: 1.7 million Class 8 trucks in US, ~$75B annual fuel spend
85 tracked efficiency technologies
Baseline 6.5-7 MPG vs 9+ MPG Run on Less target

title: Run On Less 2017 – NYC Mid Run Results
abstract: NYC mid-run press event for the 2017 Run on Less campaign, featuring RMI's Jules Kortenhorst, Richard Branson, NACFE's Mike Roeth, PepsiCo's Mike O'Connell, and Shell's Dr. Selda Gunsel discussing the campaign's headline result -- a 10.1 MPG average across the seven fleets -- and its industry significance.
key_findings: Mid-run results reported a 10.1 MPG average across the seven Run on Less fleets, cited by PepsiCo's Mike O'Connell as a significant real-world fuel-efficiency improvement.
data_available: 10.1 MPG average across seven fleets (mid-run figure)

title: 2017 Stories – Drop and Hook
abstract: Explainer segment using 2017 Run on Less examples to illustrate the drop-and-hook trailer-swap practice common in trucking, where mismatched tractor/trailer aerodynamic technology can erase fuel savings. Mike Roeth and driver Clark Reed describe how losing aero components like trailer tails can cost 10-15% in fuel economy.
key_findings: Mike Roeth states that swapping from a highly efficient trailer to one without efficiency technologies can cost 10-15% in fuel economy, roughly $4,000 per year in fuel cost.
Clark Reed (Nussbaum) describes losing about half a mile per gallon when hauling a trailer without a trailer tail, plus further losses from dual (vs. wide-base) tires and no eco flaps.
data_available: 10-15% MPG difference between efficient vs. standard trailer (drop-and-hook)
~$4,000/year estimated fuel cost impact
~0.5 MPG loss without trailer tail

title: Run On Less 2017 – Kick-Off
abstract: Official kickoff video for the September 2017 Run on Less campaign, introducing all seven participating Class 8 fleets and drivers -- Ploger, Nussbaum, Albert Transport, Mesilla Valley, Frito-Lay, Hirschbach, and US Xpress -- hauling real freight on real routes while Geotab telematics streamed live data to runonless.com.
key_findings: Seven fleets/drivers -- Ploger, Nussbaum, Albert Transport, Mesilla Valley Transportation, Frito-Lay, Hirschbach, and US Xpress -- were equipped with Geotab telematics devices for the first-of-its-kind Run on Less fuel-economy showcase.

title: 2017 Stories – Supertrucks
abstract: Mike Roeth compares the 2017 Run on Less trucks to the DOE SuperTruck program (circa 2009, teams led by Cummins/Peterbilt and Navistar/Daimler/Volvo), explaining that Run on Less trucks approach SuperTruck-level MPG despite lighter design weight and fewer exotic technologies like waste heat recovery.
key_findings: DOE SuperTruck demonstrators achieved 11-13 MPG under a 65,000 lb design weight limit; Run on Less trucks approach similar fuel economy levels using currently production-available technology, generally at lower operating weights.
data_available: DOE SuperTruck MPG range (11-13 MPG)
DOE SuperTruck design weight limit (65,000 lb)

title: 2017 Stories – Solar
abstract: Segment on solar panels for Class 8 tractors and trailers as an emerging technology to power hotel loads (A/C, lights, batteries) and reduce idling and dead-battery issues. Drivers Mark Risien and Allan Dahringer describe positive experience with roof-mounted solar-charged APU battery packs; NACFE previews a 2018 Solar Confidence Report.
key_findings: Driver Allan Dahringer ran his APU continuously for 12+ hours on solar-charged batteries with no issue starting the truck afterward.
NACFE announced a Solar Confidence Report to be published in 2018 at truckingefficiency.org.

title: Run On Less 2017 – NBC Coverage
abstract: Fort Wayne NBC news segment (reporter Kent Hormann) on the September 2017 Run on Less campaign, featuring Mike Roeth and Dave Schaller explaining the goal of showcasing seven fleets achieving 9+ MPG versus the 4-5 MPG typical of less-efficient trucks, tying fuel efficiency to lower consumer prices and emissions.
key_findings: Mike Roeth notes the featured drivers are achieving 9+ MPG, intended to influence other truckers still averaging 4-5 MPG.

title: 2017 Stories – Traffic & Congestion
abstract: Segment on how road congestion -- urban traffic, accidents, construction, and hurricane evacuations -- erodes fuel economy during the 2017 Run on Less, illustrated by driver anecdotes from California traffic and a Hurricane Irma evacuation slowdown on I-95, plus an ATRI industry-wide congestion cost statistic.
key_findings: Mike Roeth cites ATRI data that congestion causes about 996 million hours of wasted truck-driver time annually, costing the industry over $63 billion.
data_available: 996 million hours/year wasted truck-driver time and $63B annual cost (ATRI, cited by NACFE)

title: 2017 Stories – Team Drivers
abstract: Mike Roeth explains how team driving (two drivers sharing a truck) improves fuel efficiency during the 2017 Run on Less by keeping the truck moving continuously and enabling long dedicated hauls, citing typical mileage output and MPG gains for team-driven trucks versus solo drivers.
key_findings: Mike Roeth states team driving can achieve up to 5,000 miles/week (1,000 miles/day) and typically yields a 0.3-0.4 MPG improvement versus solo driving.
data_available: Team driving weekly/daily mileage (up to 5,000 mi/week, 1,000 mi/day)
0.3-0.4 MPG improvement from team driving

title: Electric Stories – Electric Truck Drivers
abstract: Short montage of Run on Less – Electric (Sept 2021) drivers giving first-person testimonials about switching to battery-electric trucks: quieter operation improves street awareness, trucks arrive each morning fully charged, and several drivers describe pride in being early adopters. No fleet names or performance data given.
key_findings: Drivers report quieter electric trucks improve situational awareness on the road (hearing surroundings, less startling to people in small towns) compared with diesel trucks.
Drivers describe pride in being early adopters and note the trucks arrive fully charged and ready each morning.

title: 2017 Stories – Freight Efficiency
abstract: Mike Roeth explains why NACFE emphasizes freight moved per gallon over raw MPG, using Frito-Lay's Run on Less truck as the example: because snack loads cube out before they gross out, Frito-Lay runs a custom drop-frame trailer (built by Kentucky Trailer) that adds 11% more cargo space.
key_findings: Frito-Lay uses a Kentucky Trailer-built drop-frame trailer that provides 11% more cargo space to address light, low-density ('cubed out') snack loads.
Roeth argues freight-efficiency metrics (freight hauled per gallon, ton-miles per gallon) are more meaningful than plain MPG for fleets that don't gross out at 80,000 lbs.

title: Run On Less – Messy Middle Breakfast at ACT Expo
abstract: ACT Expo 2025 breakfast event where Mike Roeth and Amanda Phillips introduce the 13 fleets running Run on Less – Messy Middle (Sept 2025), spanning diesel/biodiesel, renewable diesel, CNG, battery-electric, and hydrogen fuel cell trucks. Each fleet representative previews their planned route, mileage, and technology ahead of the demonstration.
key_findings: Kleysen Group will run 143,000 lbs on an 8-axle natural-gas trailer over a 600-mile daily round trip reaching 56°N latitude, spanning recorded temperatures from 104°F to -63°F.
4Gen Logistics operates 83 trucks (64 battery-electric, 15 hydrogen fuel cell, 3 CNG, remainder diesel) and expects to be fully zero-emission by the end of 2025.
data_available: Per-fleet route mileage, vehicle spec, and powertrain listing (13 fleets)

title: 2025 Run on Less – Messy Middle
abstract: Promotional trailer for Run on Less – Messy Middle (2025), tracing NACFE's Run on Less history from 2017 through 2025 and listing the 13 participating Messy Middle fleets by powertrain (diesel/biodiesel, renewable diesel, CNG, battery-electric, hydrogen fuel cell). Previews August fleet profiles, the September 18-day run, and upcoming reports.
key_findings: 13 fleets are confirmed for Run on Less – Messy Middle (Sept 2025): Albert Transport, Mesilla Valley Transportation, Frito-Lay, J.B. Hunt, Kleysen Group, UPS, Wegmans, 4Gen Logistics, Joyride Logistics, Nevoya, Saia, Penske, and Pilot.
NACFE plans Total Cost of Ownership, Environmental Impact, and Operational Impact reports from the run, to be released October 2025 through June 2026.
data_available: List of 13 confirmed Messy Middle fleets with powertrain and location

title: 2017 Stories – Fuel Economy on Older Equipment
abstract: Mike Roeth profiles two veteran owner-operators outside the official Run on Less roster — Steve Crone and Alec Caseras, both driving for Landstar — who achieve high fuel economy on older trucks through aggressive aerodynamic modifications (nose cones, side skirts, custom tails), lift axles, and driver-coaching feedback tools.
key_findings: Steve Crone gets roughly 10 MPG on a 15-year-old International truck using a modified 2017 Mack front end, a self-invented tail, and by removing non-essential drag items like the license plate and grab handles.
Alec Caseras (Landstar) uses a nose cone, a Windyne Fairing side skirt with a flip-and-slide feature, a lift axle, and driver-coaching feedback tools to reach double-digit fuel economy.

title: 2017 Stories – Trucking Efficiency Operation
abstract: Overview of NACFE's Trucking Efficiency initiative (with Carbon War Room): North American fleets spend $105B/year on fuel, averaging ~$70,000 per truck/year, with 30-50% potential savings across 70 identified efficiency technologies. Describes the confidence-report methodology for producing objective, third-party technology assessments.
key_findings: NACFE estimates North American tractor-trailer fleets spend $105 billion/year on fuel (~$70,000 per truck/year at 125,000 miles), with up to $40 billion/year in potential industry-wide savings.
Trucking Efficiency has identified 70 distinct fuel-efficiency technologies for tractor-trailers and produces confidence reports assessing their fuel savings.
data_available: $105B industry fuel spend estimate
70-technology efficiency catalog reference

title: Run on Less Profiles – US Xpress, Inc.
abstract: Fleet profile of US Xpress driver Mark Risien (Tunnel Hill, GA, driving since the 1980s), showcasing his 2017 Run on Less truck's fuel-saving equipment: solar panel, dual battery banks for hotel loads, automatic tire inflation, wheel covers, low rolling resistance tires, tandem drive fairings, side skirt, cab extenders, and a rear TopKit.
key_findings: Driver Mark Risien's truck combines a solar panel with dual battery banks to power cab electronics/HVAC without idling, plus a full aerodynamic package (side skirt, tandem drive fairings, cab extenders, TopKit) and automatic tire inflation.

title: Run on Less Profiles – Ploger Transportation
abstract: Fleet profile of Ploger Transportation driver Joel Morrow (Bellevue, OH, 30 years driving, ~530 miles/day multi-stop furniture routes), spec'ing an 11-liter engine for lower rotating mass, a Wall-Bash AeroFin XL trailer tail, low rolling resistance tires, electronic logs, an OBD reader, and a pedal-coach fuel-flow device.
key_findings: Joel Morrow's truck uses an 11-liter engine (instead of 13L/15L) for less rotating mass, and reports the Wall-Bash AeroFin XL trailer tail gains about 0.3-0.4 MPG.
Truck uses low rolling resistance tires on free-rolling positions but a higher-rolling-resistance drive tire, which Morrow found works better in the fleet's 6x2 applications.

title: Run on Less Profiles – PepsiCo's Frito-Lay Division
abstract: Fleet profile of Frito-Lay driver Tommy Revell (Perry, GA, 32 years driving, ~540-mile Charleston, SC route) and fleet sustainability manager Ken Marko, describing the fleet's shift from ~4.5-5 MPG cab-over trucks to ~9.5 MPG via idle shutdown, two-speed fans, downsped AMTs, and a full aerodynamic package.
key_findings: Frito-Lay's fuel economy rose from about 4.5-5 MPG on older cab-over trucks (13 years prior) to about 9.5 MPG on current equipment, per driver Tommy Revell.
Fleet uses idle shutdown systems, two-speed fan drives, downsped automated manual transmissions, and a full aero package (lower-dam bumpers, side skirts, gap fairings, wheel covers, trailer tails).

title: Run on Less Profiles – Nussbaum
abstract: Fleet profile of Nussbaum Transportation driver Clark Reed (Roscoe, IL, ~12.5 years driving), detailing his 2018 Freightliner Cascadia Evolution's fuel-saving tech: predictive/adaptive cruise, low bumper, low rolling resistance tires, 6x2 axle, 29-foot trailer skirts, automatic tire inflation, EcoFlaps, trailer tails, battery APU, and a DD15/DT12 powertrain.
key_findings: Nussbaum financially rewards drivers for fuel-saving driving habits; driver Clark Reed's DD15 (400hp) engine paired with the DT12 automated transmission cruises at about 1,175 RPM.
Truck and trailer equipped with a 6x2 axle, 29-foot trailer skirts, automatic tire inflation, EcoFlaps, trailer tails, and a battery-electric APU for HVAC/power.

title: Run on Less Profiles – Mesilla Valley Transportation
abstract: Fleet profile of Mesilla Valley Transportation driver Roberto Sandoval (El Paso, TX, 26 years driving) and maintenance director Allan Dahringer, detailing a 2018 International LT with Cummins X15 (430hp), two-speed fan clutch, aero mirrors, solar-charged 8-battery APU bank, full fairings/skirts, wheel covers, and a Wabash multi-section skirt.
key_findings: Truck runs a 6x2 axle configuration with a full aero package achieving a roughly 23-23.5 inch tractor-to-trailer gap, plus an 8-battery bank (4 for start, 4 for APU) charged by roof-mounted solar.

title: Run on Less Profiles – Hirschbach
abstract: Fleet profile of Hirschbach driver Brad Long (Indiana, 12 years/1.3M miles) and John Vesey on the fleet's green strategy: trucks kept to 3-4 years old, trailers to 5 years, with Bendix Wingman adaptive cruise, tire pressure sensors, Michelin low rolling resistance tires, trailer skirts, lightweight aluminum components, and a TriPac Evolution diesel APU.
key_findings: Hirschbach keeps its truck fleet to 3-4 years old and trailers to 5 years old to reduce maintenance costs and improve fuel economy, per John Vesey.
Truck equipped with Bendix Wingman adaptive cruise control, tire pressure sensors, Michelin low rolling resistance tires, trailer skirts, and lightweight aluminum components.

title: Run on Less Profiles – Albert Transportation Inc.
abstract: Fleet profile of owner-operator Henry Albert (Albert Transport, independent since 1996, driving since 1983) walking through his 2018 Freightliner Cascadia AeroX: DD15 downsped engine (400hp, 1,750 lb-ft torque at ~975 RPM), micro-polished DT12 gears, NoseCone, side skirts, trailer tail, and a relocated license plate estimated to save $400-700/year in fuel.
key_findings: Henry Albert calculated that a trailer license plate mounted in the airstream costs $400-700/year in extra fuel (at $3.70/gallon) versus his relocated position.
Truck's Detroit DD15 downsped engine produces 400 hp / 1,750 lb-ft torque, peaking around 975 RPM, paired with a micro-polished DT12 transmission to reduce parasitic drag.

title: Run on Less 2017 – Recap
abstract: Closing recap of the original 2017 Run on Less: seven drivers covered 50,107 total miles over a 17-day event (99 combined driving days), averaging 10.1 MPG — beating NACFE's pre-run 9 MPG expectation — despite hurricanes Harvey and Irma disrupting freight during the run. Richard Branson appears at the closing event.
key_findings: The seven 2017 Run on Less trucks covered 50,107 total miles over 17 days (99 combined driver-days) and averaged 10.1 MPG, exceeding NACFE's pre-run expectation of 9 MPG.
data_available: Aggregate run totals: 50,107 miles, 10.1 MPG average, 17 days / 99 driving days

title: Regional Stories – Growth in Regional Haul
abstract: NACFE explains why regional haul is growing ahead of Run on Less Regional (2019): e-commerce and better load-matching/routing technology are shortening average length of haul, fleets are adopting relay/team-swap models to get drivers home nightly, and predictable regional routes make natural gas, electric, and hydrogen infrastructure investment lower-risk.
key_findings: NACFE frames regional haul's predictable, dedicated routes as a lower-risk proving ground for alternative-fuel infrastructure (natural gas, electric, hydrogen) since fueling/charging locations can be planned around known routes.

title: Regional Stories – Measuring Efficiency
abstract: Explains the Run on Less Regional (2019) measurement methodology: Geotab telematics on all 10 trucks plus Oak Ridge National Lab and NREL data loggers estimate payload and account for the 'diminishing load' duty cycle of multi-stop regional routes; results are reported as a fleet-wide average MPG/ton-miles-per-gallon versus a national benchmark.
key_findings: 10 regional-haul trucks were instrumented with Geotab telematics devices, plus NREL data loggers (partnering with Oak Ridge National Laboratory) to estimate payload and characterize diminishing-load duty cycles.
Results were reported as an aggregate fleet average MPG and ton-miles-per-gallon (not individual truck MPGs) benchmarked against a national regional-haul average; a full report was expected in 2020.
data_available: Live dashboard metrics: gallons/dollars/CO2 saved, ton-miles/gallon, avg speed, avg payload

title: Regional Stories – Various Duty Cycles
abstract: Mike Roeth categorizes the 10 Run on Less Regional (2019) trucks into three duty-cycle patterns: A-B-A (point-to-point relay/trailer swaps), hub-and-spoke (multi-stop routes varying by day), and A-B-C-D-A (diminishing-load, multi-drop routes), illustrating why fleets must spec trucks flexibly rather than for one route profile.
key_findings: NACFE identifies three regional-haul duty-cycle patterns among the 2019 Run on Less Regional trucks: A-B-A (relay/trailer-swap), hub-and-spoke (multi-stop, varying daily), and A-B-C-D-A (diminishing-load, multi-drop).

title: Regional Stories – Drivers Like Regional Haul
abstract: Drivers and fleet leaders from several Run on Less Regional fleets explain why they favor regional haul: predictable nightly home time, lower driver turnover, and the familiarity and relationships built from repeat routes and regular customer stops. One executive says regional-haul turnover runs in the single digits versus 80-90% for long-haul truckload carriers.
key_findings: A fleet VP states regional-haul driver turnover is in the single digits, compared to an industry average of 80-90% for long-haul truckload carriers.
Drivers cite consistent home time, route familiarity, and relationships with store/vendor staff as the top reasons they prefer regional haul over long-haul.

title: Regional Stories – Maintenance in Regional Haul
abstract: Dave Schaller and fleet staff discuss how regional haul's return-to-base operation enables nightly vehicle inspections and maintenance at a home terminal, unlike long-haul trucks that may go months between shop visits. Southeastern Freight Lines' Atlanta shop is cited as one of the carrier's largest, with about 45 technicians across 27 fleet shops.
key_findings: Southeastern Freight Lines' VP of Fleet Services says its 27-shop network includes a full Atlanta shop with about 45 technicians handling all tractor and trailer maintenance, including engine rebuilds.
Because regional trucks return to base daily, spec changes like maximum vehicle speed can be rolled out to a fleet in days or weeks, versus 6 months to a year for long-haul fleets.

title: Regional Stories – Powertrain Technologies
abstract: Fleet engineers describe how regional haul's varied duty cycles are met with tailored powertrain specs. C&S Wholesale Grocers runs 11-, 13-, and 15-liter engines with down-sped engine/transmission pairings and lower rear-axle ratios tuned by route, while Southeastern Freight Lines has shifted from 6x4 to 6x2 and now 4x2 tractors pulling pup trailers for better fuel economy.
key_findings: C&S Wholesale Grocers runs 11-, 13-, and 15-liter engines with down-sped engine/transmission combinations and lower rear-axle ratios customized by route (mountains, heavy/light loads, climate).
Southeastern Freight Lines has progressively shifted its tractor spec from 6x4 to 6x2 to 4x2, citing significantly better fuel economy for pup-trailer (twin 28-foot) operations.

title: Regional Stories – Sleepers vs. Daycabs in Regional
abstract: Mike Roeth explains that daycabs now make up 45% of Class 8 tractors produced, and dominate regional haul, but roughly four of the ten Run on Less Regional duty cycles still run sleepers -- often for occasional overnight layovers, driver flexibility, or to standardize one truck spec across a location, as at C&S Wholesale Grocers and J.B. Hunt.
key_findings: Mike Roeth states 45% of Class 8 tractors produced go into daycab configuration.

NACFE found about four of the ten Run on Less Regional duty cycles run sleepers even though only one or two truly need them, often for occasional overnight layovers or to keep one common truck spec at a location.

title: Regional Stories – Backhauls in Regional Haul
abstract: Dave Schaller and fleet staff discuss backhaul strategies that eliminate empty return miles in regional haul. PepsiCo's Cesar Esparza describes using sister companies and carrier partners to fill return trailers, while other fleets set a minimum outbound distance -- around 500 miles from home -- before seeking a backhaul load to make the return trip worthwhile.
key_findings: PepsiCo's Cesar Esparza says the fleet uses sister companies (Freeto, TLCI) and carrier partners to find return freight and eliminate empty miles.
Some Run on Less fleets set a minimum outbound distance, roughly 500 miles from home, before pursuing a backhaul load.

title: Regional Stories – Customer Service in Regional Haul
abstract: Regional-haul drivers describe acting as informal customer-service representatives, often helping load or unload freight at stores and vendor locations they visit repeatedly. J.B. Hunt's dedicated Corsicana Mattress driver, Dustin, personally unloads every mattress and foundation by hand, including in un-vented trailers during summer heat.
key_findings: Drivers describe regularly helping load/unload freight at customer stops, beyond just driving, and building name-level relationships with recurring store and vendor contacts.
J.B. Hunt's Corsicana Mattress driver Dustin manually unloads every mattress and foundation from un-vented trailers, described as extremely hot in summer months.

title: Regional Stories – Aerodynamics at Lower Speeds
abstract: Mike Roeth and Dave Schaller counter the myth that trailer aerodynamics only matter above 50 mph, citing EPA SmartWay/SAE testing (SAE 2016-01-8133) showing benefits at 20-40 mph too. An unequipped trailer loses roughly 10% fuel economy to headwind drag; a device worth 5% at 65 mph may still deliver about 3% at 40 mph.
key_findings: Citing SAE 2016-01-8133 (Waltzer et al.) EPA SmartWay data, aerodynamic devices show measurable fuel-savings benefit even at 20-40 mph, not just highway speeds.
Mike Roeth estimates a device delivering 5% fuel benefit at 65 mph may still deliver roughly 3% at 40 mph; an unequipped dry van/reefer trailer loses about 10% fuel economy to headwind drag.
data_available: fuel-savings % vs. speed chart (SAE 2016-01-8133, ECU-based and gravimetric data)

title: Regional Stories – Drop and Hook in Regional Haul
abstract: Hirschbach driver Mark Casey describes running six drop-and-hooks a day (about 30 trailers a week) between Monterey and Lebanon, Tennessee, all without waiting on loading. Mike Roeth notes trailer telematics increasingly helps drivers locate trailers, and that automated fifth-wheel and landing-gear engagement could further speed drop-and-hook operations.
key_findings: Hirschbach driver Mark Casey runs three loaded and three empty round trips daily between Monterey, TN and Lebanon -- six drop-and-hooks a day, about 30 trailers a week, all drop-and-hook.
Mike Roeth says telematics devices on trailers are helping fleets locate trailers more reliably, reducing delays from misplaced trailers.

title: Regional Stories – Technologies to Help Drivers Get Better MPG
abstract: Mike Roeth notes driver behavior can account for roughly 30% of a truck's fuel economy, worth $10,000-$20,000 a year. Drivers and fleet staff describe technologies that help: Bluetooth pedal-coaching devices with green/yellow/red feedback, in-cab cameras, ELD messaging systems, and C&S Wholesale Grocers' fleet-wide disc brakes, collision mitigation, and lane-departure warning.
key_findings: Mike Roeth states driver behavior can account for about 30% of a truck's fuel economy, equivalent to $10,000-$20,000 in fuel per truck per year.
Fleets use a Bluetooth-connected pedal-coaching device with a green/yellow/red indicator to curb aggressive accelerator use, alongside in-cab cameras and ELD/Qualcomm messaging systems.
data_available: estimated annual fuel-cost impact of driver behavior ($10,000-$20,000/truck)

title: Regional – Finale
abstract: NACFE's campaign wrap-up: over 18 days, 10 regional-haul fleets logged 135 total driving days averaging 8.3 mpg versus a 6.0 mpg national average, saving 2,750 gallons of fuel. Scaled to 800,000 North American regional trucks, that efficiency level would save over $9 billion in fuel and 30.5 million tons of CO2 annually.
key_findings: Across 18 days and 135 total driving days with 10 fleets, average fuel economy was 8.3 mpg versus a 6.0 mpg national average, saving 2,750 gallons of fuel over the run.
Mike Roeth states that if all 800,000 North American regional-haul trucks drove at this efficiency level, the industry would save over $9 billion/year in fuel and 30.5 million tons of CO2.
data_available: average mpg (8.3) vs. national baseline (6.0)
gallons of fuel saved during the run (2,750)
extrapolated industry-wide fuel cost and CO2 savings

title: Regional Profiles – United Parcel Service
abstract: UPS profile: the Phoenix feeder operation runs about 170 tractors (roughly 100 CNG, 70 diesel) and 300-310 package cars. Newer tractors add side air dams and a deployable tractor-trailer gap-closing 'truck wing,' plus SmartWay-rated trailer tires and frequent tire-pressure checks, all aimed at incremental fuel-economy gains across the fleet.
key_findings: UPS's Phoenix, AZ feeder terminal runs about 170 tractors (about 100 CNG, 70 diesel) and 300-310 package cars, maintained on-site.
Newer UPS tractors add side air dams and a deployable 'truck wing' that closes the tractor-trailer gap at highway speed, plus SmartWay-rated tires and regular tire-pressure checks for fuel savings.
data_available: fleet composition (CNG vs. diesel tractor counts)
package car and tractor counts at the terminal

title: Regional Profiles – Southeastern Freight Lines
abstract: Southeastern Freight Lines profile: the LTL carrier spends about $400,000/day on fuel, so a 0.1 mpg gain is worth roughly $2 million. It favors single-axle (4x2) tractors pulling 28-foot pup trailers over tandem trucks (which burn 10-12 more gallons per run), with drivers swapping loads at midpoints to avoid overnight stays.
key_findings: Southeastern Freight Lines spends about $400,000/day on fuel, so a 0.1 mpg efficiency gain is worth roughly $2 million to the company (per VP Kerry Stritt).

As an LTL carrier that cubes out rather than maxes weight, Southeastern favors single-axle (4x2) tractors pulling 28-foot pup trailers; a driver notes a tandem-axle truck burns about 10-12 more gallons per run pulling twins.
data_available: daily fuel spend and dollar value of a 0.1 mpg gain
fuel gallons: single-axle vs. tandem on pup trailers

title: Regional Profiles – Schneider
abstract: Schneider profile: the fleet specs a Freightliner Cascadia with a 400-hp DD15 engine and DT12 12-speed automated transmission, plus cab extenders, aero wheel covers, axle panels, and trailer side skirts. Diesel or battery-electric APUs cut idle time, and drivers are financially incentivized for good fuel economy.
key_findings: Schneider's regional spec is a next-gen Freightliner Cascadia (P4) with a 400-hp, 1,850 lb-ft DD15 engine, DT12 12-speed AMT, and low-ratio rear end.
The tractor adds full cab extenders, aerodynamic wheel covers, inter-drive axle panels, and trailer side skirts, and uses diesel or battery-powered APUs to reduce idle.
data_available: engine spec: DD15 400 hp / 1,850 lb-ft torque

title: Regional Profiles – Ploger Transportation
abstract: Ploger Transportation profile: the fleet specs Volvo VNR tractors with D11 engines, I-Shift transmissions, and a 6x2 liftable-axle configuration that raises under light loads. Trailers use FlowBelow aero components and Yokohama 703L tires; drivers use a Bluetooth pedal-coaching device giving green/yellow/red feedback on accelerator aggressiveness.
key_findings: Ploger specs the Volvo VNR with a D11 engine and I-Shift transmission in a 6x2 liftable-axle configuration, where the second drive axle automatically raises under lighter loads to reduce tire/brake wear.
Trailers run FlowBelow underbody aero devices and Yokohama 703L tires chosen for frequent stopping, starting, and tight turns typical of regional haul.

title: Regional Profiles – Meijer
abstract: Meijer profile: SmartWay certified since 2009, the fleet's daycabs run aero skirts, hubcaps, and mud flaps, downsized 50/80-gallon tanks, a 6x4 241 rear axle, a DD13/DT12 driveline with progressive shifting, and a Posi-Lift axle. Reefer trailers use a Tier 4 diesel-electric hybrid unit (electric while docked) with a battery-topping solar panel.
key_findings: Meijer has been SmartWay certified since 2009 and specs a daycab with aero skirts, hubcaps, and mud flaps, downsized fuel tanks (80/50 gal, down from 100), a 6x4 241 rear axle, and a Posi-Lift axle that raises under about 18,000 lbs.

Reefer trailers run a Tier 4 diesel-electric hybrid unit that switches to cheaper electric power when plugged in at a dock, plus a solar panel to maintain battery charge and avoid needless diesel-engine cycling.
data_available: fuel tank downsizing (100 gal to 80/50 gal)
rear axle ratio (241, 6x4)

title: Regional Profiles – PepsiCo
abstract: PepsiCo profile filmed in Sacramento, CA. The captured transcript is limited to title cards and speaker introductions -- driver Lou Martinez, LD&T Coordinator Cesar Esparza, and fleet sustainability managers Ken Marko and Adrian Rodriguez -- with no additional dialogue or technical detail recorded in the source.
key_findings: The source transcript for this PepsiCo profile captures only intro/title cards and speaker name/title lower-thirds (driver, LD&T Coordinator, two fleet sustainability managers) filmed in Sacramento, CA; no further dialogue or technical spec detail was captured.

title: Regional Profiles – J.B. Hunt
abstract: J.B. Hunt profile: the dedicated Corsicana Mattress account runs 55 trucks and 55 drivers hauling 150-200 mattresses per load out of Texas. Tractors spec a 400-hp Cummins X15 Efficiency Series engine with an Eaton UltraShift 10-speed AMT, low-rolling-resistance tires, composite side skirts, and a shortened cab-to-axle length worth about a 1% MPG gain.
key_findings: J.B. Hunt's dedicated Corsicana Mattress account (DCS) runs 55 trucks and 55 dedicated drivers, hauling 150-200 mattresses per load with on-site fleet management.

Tractors spec a 400-hp Cummins X15 Efficiency Series engine with an Eaton UltraShift 10-speed AMT for predictive cruise control; a shortened cab-to-axle length that tightens the trailer gap is credited with about a 1% MPG gain.
data_available: fleet size (55 trucks/drivers)
MPG gain from shortened cab-to-axle length (~1%)

title: Regional Profiles – Hogan Transportation
abstract: Profile of Hogan Transportation driver Glen Williams, 25-year veteran who now runs regional routes to St. Louis and Kansas City from Hogan's 24/7 Bridgeton, Missouri terminal, hauling dedicated freight for customers like Procter & Gamble and Anheuser-Busch, using mostly International and Freightliner tractors.
key_findings: Hogan Transportation operates a 24/7 terminal in Bridgeton, Missouri, running primarily International and Freightliner tractors, with fuel-island bumper-to-mud-flap inspections on returning vehicles and fuel savings as the top operational priority.
Driver Glen Williams shifted from coast-to-coast long-haul to regional runs, letting him be home nightly after 12-14 hour days, five days a week.

title: Regional Profiles – Hirschbach
abstract: Hirschbach profile: driver Mark Casey runs three round trips daily (30 trailers/week) hauling processed chicken between Monterey, TN and Lebanon. Fleet Support Coordinator John Vesey details Hirschbach's SmartWay-certified aero package (FlowBelow, cab extenders, trailer skirts), wide-base tires, 15-liter engines with automated manual transmissions, and a solar-panel pilot on reefer units.
key_findings: Hirschbach has won the EPA SmartWay Excellence Award three years running and equips reefer tractors/trailers with FlowBelow aero devices, cab extenders, trailer skirts, and wide-base tires that save about 100 lbs per tire.
Hirschbach is piloting solar panels on refrigerated trailer units to keep batteries and GPS monitoring powered when the reefer engine is off.
data_available: fuel-saving device list (aero, tires)
trailer weight savings (~100 lbs/tire)

title: Regional Profiles – C&S Wholesale Grocers
abstract: C&S Wholesale Grocers (Winn-Dixie distribution) profile: driver Louis Scaruffi (42 years driving, 3M+ safe miles) and site manager David Hastings describe multi-stop regional routes from Baton Rouge, LA to Panama City, FL. Fleet exec Chris Trajkovski details a 2016 asset-replacement strategy adding disc brakes, collision mitigation, and lane-departure warning fleet-wide.
key_findings: C&S Wholesale Grocers' 2016 asset replacement strategy equipped tractors and trailers with disc brakes, collision mitigation, and lane departure warning, and the fleet is now working to close the tractor-trailer aerodynamic gap and improve MPG scorecarding.
Driver Louis Scaruffi has 42 years of driving experience (38 with Winn-Dixie/C&S) with over 3 million safe miles.
data_available: driver safety record (3M+ safe miles)

title: Electric Stories – Running in the Real World
abstract: Series introduction to Run on Less Electric 'Stories from the Road,' NACFE's 18-day daily video series following early battery-electric truck adopters. Frames the real-world context (weather, hours-of-service, costs, competition) and previews recurring themes: infrastructure challenges exceeding expectations, industry collaboration, and rapid expected improvement in electric trucks.
key_findings: This is the series trailer for NACFE's 18-part 'Stories from the Road' video series documenting the real-world operation of battery-electric trucks across multiple early-adopter fleets during Run on Less Electric 2021.
A recurring theme highlighted is that charging infrastructure proved more challenging to deploy than the electric trucks themselves.

title: Electric Stories – Range & Weight Anxiety
abstract: Thematic overview of range and weight anxiety for electric trucks across Run on Less Electric duty cycles: terminal tractors, tight-radius local delivery, and regional lanes under 200km/day. NACFE's Mike Roeth concludes range and weight are non-issues for the fleet duty cycles studied: city delivery, last-mile, local regional haul, and yard tractors.
key_findings: NACFE's Mike Roeth states that range and weight were not an issue for any of the Run on Less Electric fleets, across duty cycles including city delivery, last-mile delivery, local regional haul, and yard tractors.
One fleet targeted lanes under 200 kilometers per day to enable return-to-base charging; another described running 50 miles out and 50 miles back per route.
data_available: route distance examples (200km/day, 50mi out/back)

title: Electric Stories – Maintenance & Uptime
abstract: Maintenance and uptime themes across Run on Less Electric fleets. OEM voices project 30-40% lower maintenance costs than diesel, given fewer moving parts, no oil changes, and no DPF regens. One electric box truck logged 99% uptime on daily pickup-and-delivery routes; Penske's full-service lease model is highlighted as key support.
key_findings: OEM sources estimate a 30-40% reduction in maintenance expenses for electric commercial vehicles versus diesel, driven by fewer moving parts and elimination of engine oil changes, transmission oil changes, and DPF regens/replacement.
One electric box truck on daily pickup-and-delivery routes, 5 days a week, achieved 99% uptime.
data_available: maintenance cost reduction estimate (30-40%)
uptime figure (99%)

title: Electric Stories – Drivers Love Electric
abstract: Montage of driver testimonials on battery-electric trucks: drivers highlight quiet cabs, smoother torque, no diesel fumes or fueling stops, better situational awareness (hearing traffic/sirens), and pride in reduced emissions. Multiple drivers across several Run on Less Electric fleets describe the switch to electric as a clear improvement over diesel.
key_findings: Multiple drivers across Run on Less Electric fleets describe electric trucks as quieter and smoother (consistent torque), and say the quiet cab improves situational awareness (able to hear ambulances/traffic) compared to diesel.
Drivers cite eliminating diesel fueling stops and fumes, plus family/community pride in operating a zero-emission vehicle, as key benefits.

title: Electric Stories – Charging Infrastructure
abstract: Overview of charging-infrastructure patterns across Run on Less Electric fleets: most sites use overnight depot charging with turnkey systems, located for driver convenience. Panelists stress starting utility conversations early and sizing facility power and chargers to fleet needs, noting most fleets rely on Level 2 or moderate DC fast charging rather than 1-megawatt charging.
key_findings: NACFE's Jessie Lund reports that despite talk of 1-megawatt charging, most Run on Less Electric fleets reliably charge using high-power Level 2 or relatively low-power DC fast chargers, typically via overnight depot charging.

Panelists recommend planning charging infrastructure (utility conversations, facility power assessment, charger and software selection) before finalizing truck specs, and accounting for utility time-of-use electricity rates.
data_available: charging power levels discussed (Level 2, DC fast, vs 1MW)

title: Electric Stories – Early Adopters
abstract: NACFE's Jessie Lund identifies three drivers behind early EV truck adoption: sustainability commitments turned into action, financial opportunity (fuel/maintenance savings ahead of full TCO parity), and driver attraction/retention. Day & Ross describes deploying 200+ hybrid-electric vehicles in 2005 and planning 1,800 electric vehicles over the next decade as part of its 'greenest carrier in Canada' goal.
key_findings: Day & Ross deployed over 200 hybrid-electric vehicles in 2005 and plans to have 1,800 electric vehicles on the road within 10 years as part of its goal to become Canada's greenest carrier.

NACFE frames early EV truck adoption as driven by three factors: sustainability/climate commitments, financial upside (maintenance and fuel savings even before full TCO parity), and driver attraction/retention.
data_available: Day & Ross EV deployment numbers (200+ in 2005, 1,800 target)

title: Electric Stories – Total Cost of Ownership
abstract: Deep dive on electric truck total cost of ownership: hard/soft cost categories and EV-specific factors like grants, incentives, LCFS credits, and residual value uncertainty. Panelists report roughly 85% better operating efficiency and 30-40% lower maintenance versus diesel, but stress infrastructure permitting delays and utility demand-charge negotiations, with several citing continued need for grant funding for years.
key_findings: One fleet reported an approximately 85% improvement in operating efficiency for its electric vehicle versus diesel, and a panelist estimates maintenance costs will drop 30-40% with electrification.

Panelists say electrification currently requires grant/incentive funding to pencil out and expect it will take about 4-5 more years before EV trucking is cost-viable without grants; California's LCFS credits already make electricity cheaper to run than diesel.
data_available: operating efficiency improvement (~85%)
maintenance cost reduction estimate (30-40%)
expected years to grant-independence (4-5 years)
expected vehicle life estimates (10-15 years electric vs 5-7 diesel yard tractor)

title: Electric Stories – Grid Resilience & Capacity
abstract: Examines grid resilience for electric truck charging amid rising power-outage risk from extreme weather. No Run on Less Electric trucks experienced outages, but panelists stress early utility engagement and backup plans (generators, battery storage, solar, diesel standby). Frito-Lay's solar-plus-grid integration, needing 3-5 megawatts of reliable utility power, is highlighted as a case study.
key_findings: None of the Run on Less Electric trucks experienced power outage issues to date, though panelists recommend backup plans (generators, battery storage, solar, diesel standby, utility arrangements).
Frito-Lay deployed close to 1 megawatt of solar and requires 3-5 megawatts of reliable utility power for its electric fleet, selling excess solar energy back to the grid.
data_available: Frito-Lay solar capacity (~1MW)
Frito-Lay power requirement (3-5MW)

title: Electric Stories – Temperature
abstract: Explains how temperature affects electric truck range and battery performance. Diesel trucks lose 5-10% fuel economy in winter versus roughly 15%+ range loss for EVs, since batteries must be kept warm and cabin heat can't rely on waste engine heat. One upper-Midwest fleet reported batteries never dropped below 70% charge even at -20 to -30 degree ambient temperatures.
key_findings: Kevin Otto estimates electric trucks see roughly 15% or more range reduction in winter, compared to a 5-10% fuel economy loss for diesel trucks, because EVs must actively heat both the cabin and the battery pack.
An upper-Midwest fleet operating in ambient temperatures of -20 to -30 degrees reported batteries never dropped below 70% state of charge.
data_available: winter range/efficiency loss estimates (diesel 5-10% vs EV ~15%+)
cold-weather battery performance data point (70% min charge at -20 to -30F)

title: Electric Stories – Warehouse Planning
abstract: Covers electric-fleet warehouse and facility planning: siting chargers for driver convenience, future-proofing capacity so parking lots aren't repeatedly torn up, and the challenge of investing in charging infrastructure on leased real estate. Also notes electric trucks can be driven indoors (no emissions) and reduce warehouse exhaust-fan needs, and suggests pairing chargers with solar or battery storage.
key_findings: Panelists note charging infrastructure investment can run into the millions of dollars, creating a planning problem when a fleet doesn't own the warehouse real estate.
Because electric trucks produce no emissions, fleets can consider driving them directly into warehouses and may need fewer exhaust fans in the facility.

title: Electric Stories – Charging Business Models
abstract: Explains three charging business models for electric fleets: self-owned-and-operated infrastructure; Charging as a Service, where a third party plans/manages charging for a pre-agreed price per kWh or mile of range; and Electrification as a Service, where a third party also owns and manages the vehicles, exemplified by Detroit's eFill solution.
key_findings: NACFE identifies three charging business models for electric fleets: self-owned-and-operated, Charging as a Service (third-party manages charging for a fixed price per kWh or per mile of range), and Electrification as a Service (third party also owns/manages the vehicles).
Daimler/Detroit's eFill charging solution is cited as an example of a manufacturer-owned charging offering designed to give customers a single point of contact for charging issues.

title: Electric Stories – Battery Technology
abstract: Reviews battery technology trends: costs and energy density are steadily improving, iron-phosphate chemistry is regaining favor for reliability, and lack of pack standardization slows OEM integration. Data points include a truck running 22+ hours on 224 kWh of lithium-ion batteries, a fleet with zero battery replacements after 5.5 years, and a 43 kWh pack rated for 61 miles of range.
key_findings: One truck runs for over 22 continuous hours on 224 kWh of lithium-ion batteries (one frame-mounted, one cab-top mounted); another fleet using lithium iron phosphate batteries has replaced zero batteries after 5.5+ years of operation.
A separate vehicle's 43 kWh battery pack is rated for a dynamometer-tested range of 61 miles, with a two-battery variant also available.
data_available: battery capacity/runtime examples (224 kWh/22+ hrs, 43 kWh/61 mi)
battery reliability data point (0 replacements in 5.5 years)

title: Electric Stories – Electric Attracts Talent
abstract: Montage on how electric trucks help attract and retain talent -- engineers, technicians, and drivers -- across Run on Less Electric fleets. Speakers describe recruiting advantages on college campuses, technicians volunteering for electrification pilot programs, and drivers (including a self-described yard driver) expressing pride in being early adopters of the technology.
key_findings: Multiple fleets and OEMs report that electric truck programs help recruit engineers, technicians, and drivers, with technicians volunteering for innovation-fleet pilot programs and younger drivers specifically drawn to operating new technology.
Speakers expect a mix of existing diesel technicians retraining for electric plus new talent entering the industry who might not have previously considered a trucking career.

title: Electric Stories – Environmental Justice
abstract: Discusses environmental justice benefits of electric trucks for communities near ports, freeways, and industrial corridors that bear disproportionate pollution. Cites that medium/heavy trucking is about 5% of on-road vehicles but roughly 20% of transportation greenhouse gas emissions, and highlights reduced noise pollution and eliminated fuel-tank/pump ground-leakage risk as added community benefits.
key_findings: Medium- and heavy-duty commercial trucks make up only about 5% of the on-road transportation fleet but account for roughly 20% of transportation greenhouse gas emissions, per Brandon Jones.
Electric trucks eliminate fuel tanks and pumps (removing ground leakage risk) and significantly reduce noise pollution in residential and urban delivery areas.
data_available: emissions share stat (5% of fleet, 20% of GHG emissions)

title: Electric Stories – Diving into Data
abstract: Overview of the Geotab-powered runonless.com telemetry platform used across Run On Less Electric, showing state of charge, energy in/out, truck activity, and distance-by-speed metrics for participating fleets. Includes brief industry testimonials (ICCT, Roush CleanTech, Shell, Lightning eMotors, Frito-Lay, Dana, Freightliner, Greenlots, Meritor) on real-world EV data and industry collaboration.
key_findings: Run on Less Electric telemetry (via Geotab) tracks state of charge vs speed/distance, energy in (charge % vs regen %), energy out (drive % vs idle %), truck activity, and distance-by-speed-range for participating fleets.

Industry representatives from ICCT, Roush CleanTech, Shell, Lightning eMotors, Frito-Lay, Dana, Freightliner, Greenlots, and Meritor frame the campaign as an education and collaboration effort providing real-world EV performance data.
data_available: state of charge vs speed/distance, energy in/out %, truck activity, and distance-by-speed-range metrics (Geotab telematics)

title: Electric Use Cases – Vans and Step Vans
abstract: NACFE overview of the van/step van market segment, estimating ~4.1 million Class 3-6 vans and step vans in the US/Canada today, growing to 8 million by 2030. Covers OEM growth, driver reactions to electric step vans (quieter, reinvented lower-floor architecture), and Level 2 overnight charging strategies across several fleets.
key_findings: NACFE estimates approximately 4.1 million Class 3-6 vans/step vans on the road in the US and Canada today, projected to reach 8 million by 2030.
Electric step vans (e.g., Workhorse C-1000) have a floor 10 inches lower than a traditional step van, reducing entry/exit from three steps to two, and use Level 2 overnight charging.
data_available: NACFE market size estimate for vans/step vans, current and 2030 projection

title: Electric Use Cases – Heavy-Duty Regional Haul Tractors
abstract: NACFE segment overview of regional-haul Class 8 BEV adoption, finding roughly half the regional-haul tractor market suited to electrification today given return-to-base, sub-200-mile routes. Fleet reps and drivers from NFI, Penske, Biagi Bros., and Anheuser-Busch discuss route lengths, cube-out weight advantages, and driver satisfaction/recruitment benefits.
key_findings: NACFE estimates about 50% of the regional-haul tractor market (roughly 468,000 tractors) is a good fit for BEVs today, given return-to-base operation and routes generally under 200 miles.
NFI's average length of haul is about 300 miles; Anheuser-Busch runs 21 electric trucks in Southern California, projected to cut CO2 by 462 tons annually.
data_available: % and count of regional-haul tractor market suited to BEVs (NACFE estimate)
fleet-specific route lengths and CO2 reduction figures (NFI, Anheuser-Busch)

title: Electric Use Cases – Terminal Tractors
abstract: NACFE overview of the electric terminal/yard tractor use case, driven by e-commerce growth. Reps from Kalmar, NFI, Ruan, Ryder, and Lonestar Specialty Vehicles explain that terminal tractors move trailers far faster than day cabs, rely on opportunity charging during breaks, and avoid diesel aftertreatment maintenance headaches.
key_findings: Electric terminal tractors reportedly move trailers 3 to 10 times faster than a day cab truck, per Kalmar's Gina Lopez.
Terminal tractor fleets use 'opportunity charging' during driver breaks and paperwork rather than dedicated charging stops, with fleets reporting no low-battery or dead-battery issues.
data_available: terminal tractor speed advantage over day cab trucks (3-10x claim)

title: Electric Use Cases – Medium-Duty Box Trucks
abstract: NACFE's medium-duty box truck use case, noting similar duty cycles and battery characteristics to vans/step vans. Covers driver feedback (Frito-Lay, Day & Ross, Roush Fenway), body lightweighting (Morgan Truck Body), and industry challenges scaling ePTO power for liftgates and refrigeration units on incomplete vehicles.
key_findings: Morgan Truck Body reports approximately 30% weight savings (roughly 1,500 lbs) on box truck bodies to help offset battery weight.
Industry reps note medium-duty box trucks face integration challenges as incomplete vehicles, especially scaling ePTO (electric power take-off) for liftgates and refrigeration.
data_available: Morgan Truck Body weight savings percentage and lbs figure

title: Electric Profiles – Servall Electric
abstract: Profile of Servall Electric, a 70-year-old Cincinnati electrical contractor, piloting a Workhorse C-1000 electric step van for deliveries and EV charger installs. Covers driver feedback, vehicle specs (102 kWh battery, lowered floor, two-motor regen setup, 150-mile range), and the company's plan to electrify its entire fleet.
key_findings: The Workhorse C-1000 step van's battery pack provides up to 102 kWh, giving about 150 miles of range.
Servall Electric, a third-generation Cincinnati electrical contractor, plans to replace its entire fleet with electric vehicles after piloting this first unit.
data_available: Workhorse C-1000 battery capacity (102 kWh) and range (150 mi)

title: Electric Profiles – NFI Freight
abstract: Profile of NFI's Volvo VNR Electric tractors hauling drayage containers between the Port of Long Beach and the Inland Empire, about 240 miles round trip daily. Covers Volvo's VNR Electric pilot (two-motor, two-speed powertrain), driver feedback, and NFI's plans to scale the program into other dedicated operations.
key_findings: NFI's Volvo VNR Electric tractors run about 240 miles round trip per day on drayage routes between the Port of Long Beach and the Inland Empire.
The VNR Electric powertrain uses two electric motors producing 340 kilowatts (455 horsepower) with a two-speed transmission, rated to pull an 82,000 lb gross combination weight.
data_available: VNR Electric route distance (240 mi round trip)
VNR Electric motor power (340 kW / 455 hp) and GCW rating (82,000 lb)

title: Electric Profiles – Roush Fenway Racing
abstract: Profile of Roush Fenway Racing's Roush CleanTech electric Ford F-650 truck, used for parts/distribution on its NASCAR campus and to local race teams within about 35 miles. Covers the team's carbon-neutral race team certification, vehicle specs, and driver feedback.
key_findings: The Roush CleanTech electric F-650 uses two 400V batteries totaling 138 kWh driving a Dana electric motor, with a 14,000 lb payload rating.
Roush Fenway Racing became the first carbon-neutral certified race team in the US, partly via electrifying its support fleet with Ford/Roush CleanTech.
data_available: Roush CleanTech F-650 battery specs (400V, 138 kWh) and payload (14,000 lb)

title: Electric Profiles – Biagi Bros
abstract: Profile of Biagi Bros. hauling wine between Sonoma and Napa on a Peterbilt 579EV tractor with a Meritor electric powertrain, run on one dedicated route. Covers driver feedback, regenerative braking on hilly terrain, and Meritor's next-generation 14Xe ePowertrain design coming to production.
key_findings: Biagi Bros. runs its Peterbilt 579EV tractor on a single dedicated route shuttling wine between a Napa warehouse and a Sonoma bottling facility.
Meritor's next-gen 14Xe ePowertrain integrates the motor and transmission into the axle, freeing frame-rail space for more battery storage versus the current pre-production prototype truck.

title: Electric Profiles – Ruan
abstract: Profile of Ruan's Orange EV electric yard tractor operating in Upper Midwest winter conditions. Covers driver feedback, battery performance in sub-zero temperatures, Orange EV's multi-year fleet history without a battery replacement, and its tiered charging speed options.
key_findings: Orange EV reports over 5.5 years of fleet experience on its lithium-ion iron phosphate battery T-series without replacing a single battery.
Ruan's battery held above 70% charge even in ambient temperatures of -20 to -30°F; Orange EV charging options range from about 10 hours (standard) to under 2 hours (fast charge).
data_available: Orange EV charge time tiers (10 hrs standard / <8 hrs enhanced / <2 hrs fast)
battery charge level retained in cold weather (>70%)

title: Electric Profiles – Purolator
